lessons.title: SLIs
lessons.summary: A service-level indicator measures a user-relevant aspect of service behavior, such as successful checkouts or response latency.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A service-level indicator measures a user-relevant aspect of service behavior, such as successful checkouts or response latency.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Define the eligible population, good-event condition and measurement location. Successful events divided by eligible events gives an availability-style SLI. Excluding difficult requests or measuring only internal components can hide real user failures.

lessons.takeaway: Define the eligible population, good-event condition and measurement location. Successful events divided by eligible events gives an availability-style SLI. Excluding difficult requests or measuring only internal components can hide real user failures.

lessons.title: SLOs
lessons.summary: A service-level objective sets a target for an SLI over an explicit evaluation window.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A service-level objective sets a target for an SLI over an explicit evaluation window.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Choose a target from user needs and the cost of reliability. For example, 99.9% successful eligible requests over 30 days leaves 0.1% unsuccessful requests. Specify low-traffic and missing-data behavior before using it for decisions.

lessons.takeaway: Choose a target from user needs and the cost of reliability. For example, 99.9% successful eligible requests over 30 days leaves 0.1% unsuccessful requests. Specify low-traffic and missing-data behavior before using it for decisions.

lessons.title: Error budgets
lessons.summary: An error budget is the unreliability allowed by an SLO.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: An error budget is the unreliability allowed by an SLO.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: For an event-based SLO, allowed bad events equal eligible events multiplied by one minus the target. A shared budget policy determines when to prioritize stabilization, slow risky releases or accept experiments. Unused budget is not a reason to ignore incidents.

lessons.takeaway: For an event-based SLO, allowed bad events equal eligible events multiplied by one minus the target. A shared budget policy determines when to prioritize stabilization, slow risky releases or accept experiments. Unused budget is not a reason to ignore incidents.

lessons.title: Incident roles
lessons.summary: Incident roles separate coordination, technical investigation and communication during an outage.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Incident roles separate coordination, technical investigation and communication during an outage.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: An incident commander prioritizes mitigation and assigns ownership; responders investigate bounded hypotheses; a communicator maintains updates. A shared timeline prevents conflicting changes and preserves decisions. Roles may be combined for small incidents but ownership should stay explicit.

lessons.takeaway: An incident commander prioritizes mitigation and assigns ownership; responders investigate bounded hypotheses; a communicator maintains updates. A shared timeline prevents conflicting changes and preserves decisions. Roles may be combined for small incidents but ownership should stay explicit.

lessons.title: Mitigation
lessons.summary: Mitigation reduces current customer impact before the full cause is understood.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Mitigation reduces current customer impact before the full cause is understood.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A known-safe rollback, traffic shift or feature disablement can restore service faster than a code-level diagnosis. Evaluate reversibility, data compatibility and capacity at the destination. Continue collecting evidence without delaying an effective recovery action.

lessons.takeaway: A known-safe rollback, traffic shift or feature disablement can restore service faster than a code-level diagnosis. Evaluate reversibility, data compatibility and capacity at the destination. Continue collecting evidence without delaying an effective recovery action.

lessons.title: Postmortems
lessons.summary: A postmortem records impact, timeline, contributing conditions and improvements after an incident.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A postmortem records impact, timeline, contributing conditions and improvements after an incident.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Blameless analysis examines why decisions made sense with the available information. Separate evidence from hypotheses, identify detection and recovery gaps, and assign concrete actions with owners and completion checks. A report without follow-through does not reduce recurrence.

lessons.takeaway: Blameless analysis examines why decisions made sense with the available information. Separate evidence from hypotheses, identify detection and recovery gaps, and assign concrete actions with owners and completion checks. A report without follow-through does not reduce recurrence.

lessons.title: Toil
lessons.summary: Toil is repetitive operational work that is automatable, reactive and tends to grow with service scale.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Toil is repetitive operational work that is automatable, reactive and tends to grow with service scale.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Measure frequency, duration and failure risk before selecting automation. Reducing the underlying need may be better than scripting every step. Valuable manual judgment and learning are not automatically toil.

lessons.takeaway: Measure frequency, duration and failure risk before selecting automation. Reducing the underlying need may be better than scripting every step. Valuable manual judgment and learning are not automatically toil.

lessons.title: Runbooks
lessons.summary: A runbook is a tested operational procedure for a recognizable condition.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A runbook is a tested operational procedure for a recognizable condition.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Include prerequisites, symptoms, evidence, decision branches, bounded actions and escalation criteria. A useful runbook tells responders when to stop as well as what to run. Assign an owner and test it against changed systems.

lessons.takeaway: Include prerequisites, symptoms, evidence, decision branches, bounded actions and escalation criteria. A useful runbook tells responders when to stop as well as what to run. Assign an owner and test it against changed systems.

lessons.title: Burn rate
lessons.summary: Burn rate compares observed bad-event rate with the rate allowed by the SLO.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Burn rate compares observed bad-event rate with the rate allowed by the SLO.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: For a 99.9% target, a 1% bad-event rate burns the budget at 10 times the sustainable rate. Combine long and short windows to detect sustained impact promptly without paging on every transient spike.

lessons.takeaway: For a 99.9% target, a 1% bad-event rate burns the budget at 10 times the sustainable rate. Combine long and short windows to detect sustained impact promptly without paging on every transient spike.

lessons.title: Latency indicators
lessons.summary: Latency indicators describe how long eligible user operations take or how often they meet a threshold.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Latency indicators describe how long eligible user operations take or how often they meet a threshold.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A mean can hide slow tail requests. Use a threshold-based good-event ratio for an SLO and percentiles for diagnosis. Define whether failed, cancelled and timed-out requests contribute so the indicator cannot improve when users fail faster.

lessons.takeaway: A mean can hide slow tail requests. Use a threshold-based good-event ratio for an SLO and percentiles for diagnosis. Define whether failed, cancelled and timed-out requests contribute so the indicator cannot improve when users fail faster.

lessons.title: Alert actionability
lessons.summary: An actionable alert identifies a condition requiring a specific, timely human response.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: An actionable alert identifies a condition requiring a specific, timely human response.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Page on user impact or imminent exhaustion with ownership, context and a runbook. Route nonurgent work to tickets. Assess whether a responder could take a useful action; a fluctuating metric alone is not a paging requirement.

lessons.takeaway: Page on user impact or imminent exhaustion with ownership, context and a runbook. Route nonurgent work to tickets. Assess whether a responder could take a useful action; a fluctuating metric alone is not a paging requirement.

lessons.title: Capacity headroom
lessons.summary: Capacity headroom is usable spare capacity relative to expected demand and failure conditions.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Capacity headroom is usable spare capacity relative to expected demand and failure conditions.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Measure the limiting resource under representative workload, including dependencies and scaling delay. Reserve enough for a planned failure domain and forecast growth. Aggregate CPU headroom does not guarantee database or connection-pool headroom.

lessons.takeaway: Measure the limiting resource under representative workload, including dependencies and scaling delay. Reserve enough for a planned failure domain and forecast growth. Aggregate CPU headroom does not guarantee database or connection-pool headroom.

lessons.title: Load shedding
lessons.summary: Load shedding intentionally rejects lower-priority or excess work to keep essential work healthy.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Load shedding intentionally rejects lower-priority or excess work to keep essential work healthy.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Reject early before expensive processing, use bounded concurrency and communicate retry behavior. Evaluate fairness and business priority. Returning controlled failures can preserve overall usefulness better than allowing every request to time out.

lessons.takeaway: Reject early before expensive processing, use bounded concurrency and communicate retry behavior. Evaluate fairness and business priority. Returning controlled failures can preserve overall usefulness better than allowing every request to time out.

lessons.title: Backpressure
lessons.summary: Backpressure communicates downstream saturation so upstream producers reduce work.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Backpressure communicates downstream saturation so upstream producers reduce work.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Bounded queues, concurrency limits and explicit rejection can propagate pressure. If upstream ignores the signal or retries aggressively, overload grows. Measure queue depth and oldest-item age to distinguish a short burst from sustained capacity shortage.

lessons.takeaway: Bounded queues, concurrency limits and explicit rejection can propagate pressure. If upstream ignores the signal or retries aggressively, overload grows. Measure queue depth and oldest-item age to distinguish a short burst from sustained capacity shortage.

lessons.title: Retry storms
lessons.summary: A retry storm occurs when repeated attempts amplify traffic to a failing dependency.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A retry storm occurs when repeated attempts amplify traffic to a failing dependency.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Retries across several layers multiply, especially when clients synchronize. Limit attempts and concurrent retries, add exponential backoff with jitter, and honor end-to-end deadlines. Recovery may require reducing retry traffic before scaling the dependency.

lessons.takeaway: Retries across several layers multiply, especially when clients synchronize. Limit attempts and concurrent retries, add exponential backoff with jitter, and honor end-to-end deadlines. Recovery may require reducing retry traffic before scaling the dependency.

lessons.title: Recovery testing
lessons.summary: Recovery testing demonstrates that backups, failover and runbooks can restore a usable service.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Recovery testing demonstrates that backups, failover and runbooks can restore a usable service.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Exercise dependencies, credentials, DNS, data integrity and user transactions in an isolated or controlled environment. Record actual recovery time and recovered data age. A successful backup job is evidence of creation, not proof of restoration.

lessons.takeaway: Exercise dependencies, credentials, DNS, data integrity and user transactions in an isolated or controlled environment. Record actual recovery time and recovered data age. A successful backup job is evidence of creation, not proof of restoration.

lessons.title: RTO
lessons.summary: Recovery time objective is the target maximum time to restore the required service capability after disruption.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Recovery time objective is the target maximum time to restore the required service capability after disruption.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Define when the clock starts and what counts as restored. Detection, decision-making, provisioning and validation all consume time. Measure complete recovery exercises against the target rather than timing only a database restore command.

lessons.takeaway: Define when the clock starts and what counts as restored. Detection, decision-making, provisioning and validation all consume time. Measure complete recovery exercises against the target rather than timing only a database restore command.

lessons.title: RPO
lessons.summary: Recovery point objective is the target maximum data loss expressed as time.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Recovery point objective is the target maximum data loss expressed as time.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Backup interval and replication lag influence the recoverable point, but consistency and accessibility also matter. Verify the actual recovered transactions. Synchronous replication can reduce some loss windows but does not protect against every logical deletion or corruption.

lessons.takeaway: Backup interval and replication lag influence the recoverable point, but consistency and accessibility also matter. Verify the actual recovered transactions. Synchronous replication can reduce some loss windows but does not protect against every logical deletion or corruption.

lessons.title: Canary releases
lessons.summary: A canary release exposes a bounded portion of traffic to a new version before wider rollout.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A canary release exposes a bounded portion of traffic to a new version before wider rollout.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Compare representative cohorts with predefined success and abort criteria. Small samples and traffic differences can mislead. Automate stopping or rollback only when the measurement and rollback path are trustworthy.

lessons.takeaway: Compare representative cohorts with predefined success and abort criteria. Small samples and traffic differences can mislead. Automate stopping or rollback only when the measurement and rollback path are trustworthy.

lessons.title: Feature flags
lessons.summary: Feature flags change behavior without requiring a new deployment.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Feature flags change behavior without requiring a new deployment.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: They enable gradual exposure and rapid disabling of risky paths. Flag services and defaults become dependencies, so define behavior during their failure. Remove obsolete flags to avoid untested combinations and permanent complexity.

lessons.takeaway: They enable gradual exposure and rapid disabling of risky paths. Flag services and defaults become dependencies, so define behavior during their failure. Remove obsolete flags to avoid untested combinations and permanent complexity.

lessons.title: Dependencies
lessons.summary: A dependency is a service or resource required for an operation's success.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A dependency is a service or resource required for an operation's success.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Map critical and optional dependencies, their timeout budgets and failure modes. Protect shared dependencies with isolation, caching or bounded fallback where semantics allow. A healthy frontend cannot compensate for an unavailable mandatory write path.

lessons.takeaway: Map critical and optional dependencies, their timeout budgets and failure modes. Protect shared dependencies with isolation, caching or bounded fallback where semantics allow. A healthy frontend cannot compensate for an unavailable mandatory write path.

lessons.title: Graceful degradation
lessons.summary: Graceful degradation preserves essential functions while reducing optional functionality under failure.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Graceful degradation preserves essential functions while reducing optional functionality under failure.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: For example, checkout may remain available while recommendations are disabled. Fallbacks need explicit correctness, freshness and capacity limits. Returning stale or incomplete data is acceptable only when the product's contract permits it.

lessons.takeaway: For example, checkout may remain available while recommendations are disabled. Fallbacks need explicit correctness, freshness and capacity limits. Returning stale or incomplete data is acceptable only when the product's contract permits it.

lessons.title: Chaos experiments
lessons.summary: A chaos experiment tests a specific resilience hypothesis by introducing a controlled failure.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A chaos experiment tests a specific resilience hypothesis by introducing a controlled failure.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Define the expected steady state, scope, observability and abort condition before injecting a fault. Start with a small blast radius and a working recovery path. Randomly breaking production without a hypothesis is not a useful experiment.

lessons.takeaway: Define the expected steady state, scope, observability and abort condition before injecting a fault. Start with a small blast radius and a working recovery path. Randomly breaking production without a hypothesis is not a useful experiment.

lessons.title: Incident communication
lessons.summary: Incident communication gives stakeholders timely, accurate information about impact and recovery.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Incident communication gives stakeholders timely, accurate information about impact and recovery.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: State what is known, what remains uncertain, current mitigation and the next update time. Avoid speculative root causes or unsupported restoration estimates. Keep technical coordination and customer-facing updates consistent without exposing unnecessary sensitive detail.

lessons.takeaway: State what is known, what remains uncertain, current mitigation and the next update time. Avoid speculative root causes or unsupported restoration estimates. Keep technical coordination and customer-facing updates consistent without exposing unnecessary sensitive detail.

lessons.title: SLO aggregation
lessons.summary: SLO aggregation combines measurements across populations or services.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: SLO aggregation combines measurements across populations or services.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Weight event-based ratios by their eligible event counts; averaging percentages gives small populations disproportionate influence. Also inspect slices such as region or tenant because a global average can conceal a severe localized failure.

lessons.takeaway: Weight event-based ratios by their eligible event counts; averaging percentages gives small populations disproportionate influence. Also inspect slices such as region or tenant because a global average can conceal a severe localized failure.

lessons.title: Overload recovery
lessons.summary: Overload recovery restores a system whose demand exceeds its effective capacity.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Overload recovery restores a system whose demand exceeds its effective capacity.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: First reduce incoming work, retries or backlog processing so recovery has room to succeed. Ramp traffic gradually and watch queues and dependency latency. Restarting every instance simultaneously can destroy caches and make overload worse.

lessons.takeaway: First reduce incoming work, retries or backlog processing so recovery has room to succeed. Ramp traffic gradually and watch queues and dependency latency. Restarting every instance simultaneously can destroy caches and make overload worse.

lessons.title: Consistency trade-offs
lessons.summary: Consistency describes which observations of distributed state clients can rely on.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Consistency describes which observations of distributed state clients can rely on.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Replication and failures create choices involving staleness, availability and coordination latency. State the consistency needed for each operation instead of labeling the whole system with one slogan. Money movement and recommendations often have different requirements.

lessons.takeaway: Replication and failures create choices involving staleness, availability and coordination latency. State the consistency needed for each operation instead of labeling the whole system with one slogan. Money movement and recommendations often have different requirements.

lessons.title: Reliability investment
lessons.summary: Reliability investment allocates engineering effort to reduce expected user impact and operational cost.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Reliability investment allocates engineering effort to reduce expected user impact and operational cost.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Compare incident frequency, severity, recovery difficulty and implementation cost. Use SLO performance and business needs to prioritize work. More redundancy can introduce complexity, so verify that it addresses the actual failure mode.

lessons.takeaway: Compare incident frequency, severity, recovery difficulty and implementation cost. Use SLO performance and business needs to prioritize work. More redundancy can introduce complexity, so verify that it addresses the actual failure mode.

lessons.title: Incident metrics
lessons.summary: Incident metrics describe detection, response, recovery and customer impact across events.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Incident metrics describe detection, response, recovery and customer impact across events.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Use consistent start and end definitions and examine distributions, severity and sample size. A lower average recovery time can mask a few catastrophic incidents. Metrics should support learning rather than incentivize reclassification or premature closure.

lessons.takeaway: Use consistent start and end definitions and examine distributions, severity and sample size. A lower average recovery time can mask a few catastrophic incidents. Metrics should support learning rather than incentivize reclassification or premature closure.

lessons.title: Safe automation
lessons.summary: Safe automation performs repeatable operations within explicit preconditions and boundaries.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Safe automation performs repeatable operations within explicit preconditions and boundaries.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Validate targets, use least privilege, bound concurrency and make retries idempotent. Include dry-run or preview, stop conditions and observable results. Automation should fail clearly when assumptions change instead of continuing across an entire fleet.

lessons.takeaway: Validate targets, use least privilege, bound concurrency and make retries idempotent. Include dry-run or preview, stop conditions and observable results. Automation should fail clearly when assumptions change instead of continuing across an entire fleet.

commands.title: Request success ratio
commands.definition: A PromQL expression computes a short-window request success ratio.
commands.purpose: Compare a defined checkout population with its availability objective.
commands.environment: Illustrative PromQL, not a shell command. Assumes a counter named http_requests_total and defines only 5xx as bad; adapt to actual user failures.
commands.interpretation: Result 0.999 means 99.9% success under this definition. No traffic can produce no usable ratio; status labels and eligibility must match instrumentation.
commands.safety: Illustrative PromQL, not a shell command. Assumes a counter named http_requests_total and defines only 5xx as bad; adapt to actual user failures.

commands.title: Error budget burn
commands.definition: Computes burn rate for a 99.9% event-based objective.
commands.purpose: Translate current failure rate into budget consumption speed.
commands.environment: Illustrative PromQL; use the same eligible population as the SLO and pair short and long windows.
commands.interpretation: 1 is the sustainable rate; 10 means ten times that rate. Zero traffic needs explicit handling.
commands.safety: Illustrative PromQL; use the same eligible population as the SLO and pair short and long windows.

commands.title: Long-window bad ratio
commands.definition: Estimates the bad-event fraction over thirty days.
commands.purpose: Review accumulated budget use rather than only current health.
commands.environment: Illustrative PromQL; long queries may be expensive and require sufficient retention or recording rules.
commands.interpretation: Compare with 0.001 for a 99.9% target; telemetry gaps and counter retention limit accuracy.
commands.safety: Illustrative PromQL; long queries may be expensive and require sufficient retention or recording rules.

commands.title: Tail latency
commands.definition: Estimates p99 from a classic Prometheus latency histogram.
commands.purpose: Check whether slow-tail behavior changed during a rollout.
commands.environment: Illustrative PromQL; metric and labels must exist, and sparse traffic makes estimates unstable.
commands.interpretation: The result is seconds; bucket boundaries determine estimation accuracy. It is not an average of instance p99 values.
commands.safety: Illustrative PromQL; metric and labels must exist, and sparse traffic makes estimates unstable.

commands.title: Traffic rate
commands.definition: Calculates total requests per second for a service.
commands.purpose: Distinguish a traffic surge from a capacity regression.
commands.environment: Illustrative PromQL; retries may be counted as requests, so define the population clearly.
commands.interpretation: rate handles counter resets per series before sum combines instances.
commands.safety: Illustrative PromQL; retries may be counted as requests, so define the population clearly.

commands.title: Queue age
commands.definition: Selects the largest reported age of pending work.
commands.purpose: Detect processing delay that a queue-length graph can conceal.
commands.environment: Illustrative application metric; confirm whether empty queues report zero or no series.
commands.interpretation: Seconds above the delivery objective indicate work waiting too long, not necessarily a failed worker.
commands.safety: Illustrative application metric; confirm whether empty queues report zero or no series.

commands.title: Dependency latency probe
commands.definition: Makes one bounded HTTP health request and reports status and total time.
commands.purpose: Compare reachability from a specific incident location.
commands.environment: Replace SERVICE with an authorized safe endpoint; do not load-test production with an uncontrolled loop.
commands.interpretation: A 200 from a shallow health endpoint does not prove the business transaction works.
commands.safety: Replace SERVICE with an authorized safe endpoint; do not load-test production with an uncontrolled loop.

commands.title: Deployment progress
commands.definition: Observes progress for a Kubernetes deployment.
commands.purpose: Check whether a recent change has completed before interpreting its health.
commands.environment: Kubernetes-backed example; read-only and requires the intended context.
commands.interpretation: A success message is controller progress; compare error and latency SLIs before declaring recovery.
commands.safety: Kubernetes-backed example; read-only and requires the intended context.

commands.title: Recent service evidence
commands.definition: Reads recent service logs on a systemd host.
commands.purpose: Build a bounded incident timeline without dumping all history.
commands.environment: Host-based example; read-only and output may contain sensitive data.
commands.interpretation: Correlate timestamps with deployment and alert times; missing logs may reflect retention.
commands.safety: Host-based example; read-only and output may contain sensitive data.

commands.title: Host saturation snapshot
commands.definition: Samples host scheduling, paging, I/O and CPU activity.
commands.purpose: Check whether a service slowdown correlates with resource pressure.
commands.environment: Linux example; a snapshot cannot establish the full incident history.
commands.expectedOutput: r b ... si so ... us sy id wa
commands.interpretation: Ignore the first since-boot average when comparing short intervals; inspect runnable tasks, swap and wait together.
commands.safety: Linux example; a snapshot cannot establish the full incident history.

commands.title: Replica readiness
commands.definition: Summarizes desired and available application replicas.
commands.purpose: Check whether traffic is being served with reduced capacity.
commands.environment: Kubernetes-backed example; read-only and dependent on controller observations.
commands.interpretation: READY compares ready with desired replicas; AVAILABLE reflects availability conditions, not end-user success.
commands.safety: Kubernetes-backed example; read-only and dependent on controller observations.

commands.title: Recent change history
commands.definition: Lists locally available commits in a recent window.
commands.purpose: Generate candidate changes to correlate with an incident.
commands.environment: Read-only; fetch deployment metadata separately and avoid assuming correlation proves cause.
commands.interpretation: Commit timestamps do not prove deployment time; map revisions to deployment records.
commands.safety: Read-only; fetch deployment metadata separately and avoid assuming correlation proves cause.

commands.title: Long-window burn rate
commands.definition: Compares the one-hour error ratio with the allowed ratio for a 99.9% SLO.
commands.purpose: Pair a sustained failure signal with a shorter window before paging.
commands.environment: PromQL; assumes 5xx defines bad eligible events and the metric has enough samples. Validate the SLI definition.
commands.interpretation: A value of 6 means six times the budget-compatible error rate, not 6% errors. A zero denominator requires a no-traffic policy.
commands.safety: PromQL; assumes 5xx defines bad eligible events and the metric has enough samples. Validate the SLI definition.

commands.title: Regional success ratio
commands.definition: Calculates success fraction separately by region.
commands.purpose: Find a failing region hidden by a healthy global average.
commands.environment: PromQL with matching region labels; choose the same eligibility and success definitions in numerator and denominator.
commands.interpretation: Each output value belongs to one region; 0.98 means a 98% success ratio for that region's eligible traffic.
commands.safety: PromQL with matching region labels; choose the same eligibility and success definitions in numerator and denominator.

commands.title: Canary error comparison
commands.definition: Compares recent error ratios grouped by deployed version.
commands.purpose: Assess whether a canary differs from the baseline.
commands.environment: PromQL; version labels and representative traffic are prerequisites. This query alone does not establish causation.
commands.interpretation: Compare ratios together with sample size and traffic mix; a low-volume version may have noisy estimates.
commands.safety: PromQL; version labels and representative traffic are prerequisites. This query alone does not establish causation.

commands.title: Traffic by region
commands.definition: Calculates request rate per region.
commands.purpose: Check load movement during failover or traffic restoration.
commands.environment: PromQL using an illustrative request counter; verify region labels and traffic eligibility.
commands.interpretation: Values are requests per second for each region; compare them with safe surviving capacity.
commands.safety: PromQL using an illustrative request counter; verify region labels and traffic eligibility.

commands.title: Unavailable scrape targets
commands.definition: Counts discovered scrape targets currently reporting a failed scrape.
commands.purpose: Check the breadth of a telemetry collection incident.
commands.environment: PromQL; this measures scraping, not direct customer availability. Add discovery/absence coverage separately.
commands.interpretation: A value of 2 means two selected targets have up=0; targets absent from discovery are not counted.
commands.safety: PromQL; this measures scraping, not direct customer availability. Add discovery/absence coverage separately.

commands.title: Backlog peak during recovery
commands.definition: Reports the largest sampled queue depth during the recent recovery window.
commands.purpose: Check whether restoring traffic creates a larger backlog than before.
commands.environment: PromQL with an example gauge; compare with queue age and worker processing rate.
commands.interpretation: The value is messages at the sampled peak; it does not measure oldest message age or processing throughput.
commands.safety: PromQL with an example gauge; compare with queue age and worker processing rate.

references.title: Backlog peak during recovery — primary documentation

commands.title: Bounded endpoint sample
commands.definition: Requests a health endpoint and prints response headers without the body.
commands.purpose: Collect status and routing evidence during a bounded incident check.
commands.environment: Sends one request; use an authorized endpoint and avoid exposing authentication headers in collected evidence.
commands.interpretation: The HTTP status and selected headers show this one response; a 200 on a shallow health endpoint may not represent critical journeys.
commands.safety: Sends one request; use an authorized endpoint and avoid exposing authentication headers in collected evidence.

commands.title: Deployment revision evidence
commands.definition: Lists retained revisions of an affected Kubernetes workload.
commands.purpose: Correlate release timing and recovery candidates during triage.
commands.environment: Read-only; confirm context and namespace before proposing rollback.
commands.interpretation: Revision numbers identify controller history, not necessarily source commits or database migration compatibility.
commands.safety: Read-only; confirm context and namespace before proposing rollback.

commands.title: Current deployment failures
commands.definition: Lists Pods outside the Running phase in one namespace.
commands.purpose: Find Pending or failed workload instances during response.
commands.environment: Read-only; complement with readiness checks because phase is not a full health model.
commands.interpretation: STATUS and NODE help separate scheduling from startup issues; Running Pods with failing readiness are not included by this filter.
commands.safety: Read-only; complement with readiness checks because phase is not a full health model.

commands.title: Recent host boot
commands.definition: Prints the host's boot time.
commands.purpose: Check whether a host restart aligns with an incident timeline.
commands.environment: Read-only Linux procps command; boot time is not application deployment time.
commands.interpretation: The timestamp is in the host's local time zone; correlate using a consistent time basis.
commands.safety: Read-only Linux procps command; boot time is not application deployment time.

commands.title: Changed release scope
commands.definition: Lists paths changed between two verified release revisions.
commands.purpose: Scope a release-related incident before reading the relevant patches.
commands.environment: Read-only; replace refs with deployed commit identities, not an assumed branch tip.
commands.interpretation: A, M and D mark added, modified and deleted paths; a filename change alone does not prove causation.
commands.safety: Read-only; replace refs with deployed commit identities, not an assumed branch tip.

commands.title: Backup archive integrity
commands.definition: Tests the gzip stream's integrity without extracting it.
commands.purpose: Catch a corrupt or incomplete compressed backup before a restore exercise.
commands.environment: Read-only but reads the full archive; follow with an isolated application-level restore and verification.
commands.expectedOutput: No output on successful integrity test
commands.interpretation: No output with exit 0 means the compressed stream passes checks; it does not establish database consistency or recoverability.
commands.safety: Read-only but reads the full archive; follow with an isolated application-level restore and verification.

debugging.title: Checkout failures with green hosts
debugging.symptom: CPU and memory look normal while customers cannot complete checkout.

steps.evidence: Define affected user operations and compare errors by region, version and dependency. Infrastructure utilization alone cannot establish service health.
Mitigate the failing path through a compatible rollback, traffic shift or feature disablement based on evidence. Establish a checkout SLI for ongoing detection.
Confirm successful end-to-end checkouts across affected cohorts and sustained recovery of the agreed SLI.

references.title: Checkout failures with green hosts — primary documentation

debugging.title: Fast error-budget burn
debugging.symptom: A service starts consuming its monthly error budget rapidly.

steps.evidence: For the illustrative 99.9% SLO, compare short and long burn windows and verify traffic is nonzero. Identify the failure cohort and recent changes.
Apply the agreed incident and budget policy, reduce impact and pause risky rollout expansion. Do not wait for the monthly average to become visibly poor.
Verify both immediate user recovery and declining sustained burn, then assign reliability work from the incident evidence.

debugging.title: Retry storm blocks recovery
debugging.symptom: A dependency remains overloaded after the original fault is repaired.

steps.evidence: Compare original user requests with downstream attempts, queue age and concurrent work. Multiple retry layers may sustain load beyond normal demand.
Reduce retry amplification, shed nonessential work and restore headroom before gradually reopening traffic.
Confirm attempts per original request, queue age and success rate stabilize without another synchronized retry surge.

references.title: Retry storm blocks recovery — primary documentation

debugging.title: Canary regression
debugging.symptom: A new version has slightly worse global metrics but severe errors for one client cohort.

steps.evidence: Compare canary and baseline populations by client, route and region. Check sample size and ensure the canary receives representative traffic.
Stop rollout and roll back or disable the affected feature if compatible. Correct canary analysis so important cohorts are not hidden by averages.
Verify the impacted cohort recovers and repeat a representative canary test before promotion.

debugging.title: Queue backlog threatens deadline
debugging.symptom: Background work grows older even though workers remain running.

steps.evidence: Compare arrival rate, completion rate, retry rate and dependency saturation. Determine whether additional workers would help or overload the bottleneck.
Throttle producers, prioritize urgent work or add measured capacity at the limiting stage. Bound retries and preserve duplicate-safe processing.
Confirm oldest-item age declines and representative jobs finish within the objective without downstream saturation.

references.title: Queue backlog threatens deadline — primary documentation

debugging.title: Conflicting incident changes
debugging.symptom: Several responders are changing production simultaneously with no shared timeline.

steps.evidence: Establish current impact and record active changes and owners. Separate uncertain hypotheses from observed evidence.
Assign incident coordination, pause conflicting changes and select one bounded mitigation at a time with a clear rollback condition.
Confirm responders share a timeline, each action has an owner and user impact is reducing before deeper diagnosis continues.

debugging.title: Backup exists but restore fails
debugging.symptom: A recovery drill discovers that database backups cannot produce a working application.

steps.evidence: Check backup integrity, database consistency, encryption keys, credentials and external dependencies. Measure how old the recoverable data actually is.
Repair the backup/restore procedure and missing dependencies, then test in isolation. Do not declare protection from backup-job success alone.
Complete representative transactions and document measured RTO/RPO against targets.

references.title: Backup exists but restore fails — primary documentation

debugging.title: Noisy alert fatigue
debugging.symptom: On-call receives repeated pages that resolve without action.

steps.evidence: Review incident outcomes, alert ownership and whether each page required a timely human action. Separate collection failures, symptoms and user-impact signals.
Remove or reroute nonactionable pages, add appropriate duration/grouping and retain actionable SLO or imminent-exhaustion alerts.
Replay historical conditions or rule tests to confirm real incidents still page promptly and benign fluctuations do not.

debugging.title: Capacity lost with one zone
debugging.symptom: A zone failure overloads the surviving instances.

steps.evidence: Compare surviving capacity, traffic distribution and dependency limits with the planned failure reserve. Scaling delay may exceed the impact tolerance.
Shed nonessential work and restore capacity in healthy zones using tested routing and scaling procedures. Avoid routing all traffic to an already saturated dependency.
Validate user SLIs and headroom under the failed-zone condition, then update capacity assumptions and exercises.

references.title: Capacity lost with one zone — primary documentation

debugging.title: Automation expands an outage
debugging.symptom: An automated remediation repeatedly restarts healthy replicas during a dependency incident.

steps.evidence: Inspect trigger conditions, scope and whether restarts improve the measured symptom. Dependency failures can make local health heuristics misleading.
Stop the harmful automation, restore serving capacity and redesign preconditions, concurrency bounds and stop rules.
Test dependency failures in a controlled environment and verify automation preserves capacity, stops on worsening signals and records actions.

references.title: Automation expands an outage — primary documentation
